audit.why: 50.94% over ~960 games at EVEN 6/10 with Riven at 8/10 carry threat is a fair read of a lane that is Olaf's for two levels and hers from two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Riven levels 2 and 3 and mark level 1 neutral, while whys[0] says Olaf wins first contact before she has any dashes charged and whys[1] says his level-2 burst beats what her shield can eat. First item is given to Riven although whys[5] says it trades back 'evenly'.
audit.why: Riven has no charged Broken Wings at level 1 and no Valor until 3; her takeover is a two-item mobility spike, not level 2.
audit.corrected: Chart re-proposed as one atomic group across both layers: Olaf, Olaf, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Riven, with ratings moved so the neutral rows read 5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Ragnarok cleanses her W stun and Q3 knockup' appears three times, plus 'Q3 stun' in wants.foe[1]. Two errors in one phrase: Ragnarok is immunity to disables held for as long as Olaf keeps attacking, not a cleanse; and Broken Wings' third cast is a knockback, not a stun, and displacement is not something the kit files let me claim Ragnarok covers. Ki Burst (W, 11s at rank 1) is her only actual stun.
audit.why: Telling the player Ragnarok removes the knockback invites him to walk into the third Broken Wings cast on purpose. Naming Q3 a 'stun' also blurs the one cooldown that actually decides the trade.
audit.corrected: Ki Burst named as the only stun with its 11s cooldown and the sequencing corrected to press Ragnarok as it lands. Q3 restated as a knockback with no Ragnarok claim attached. Valor named as the 10s dash-and-block that must be baited, Blade of the Exile as the AD/range steroid with a single Wind Slash.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Ki Burst' eight times with no duration.
audit.why: 11s at rank 1 is the window the entire trade pattern hangs on, and Valor's 10s is the second bait.
audit.corrected: Both written into the cooldown breakdown, the do's entry, the interactions line and the all-in window.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] prescribes 'Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.' Riven has no healing in her kit; the only sustain she gets is from runes.
audit.why: Buying anti-heal into a champion with no heal wastes a component slot in a lane the player needs armour for.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal line replaced with armour priority against an all-physical burst kit.
sources: brief enemyKit — no heal flag on any Riven ability

notes: PACKET DEFECT: brief top-level games is 977, packet.games is 958. Corrections: 'Ragnarok cleanses her W stun and Q3 knockup' appeared three times — Ragnarok is immunity to disables held while attacking, not a cleanse, and Broken Wings' third cast is a knockback, which the kit files give me no basis to say Ragnarok covers, so that half of the claim was dropped rather than reversed. wants.foe[1] also called Q3 a stun; Ki Burst is her only stun. Separately, report[8] told the player to rush Executioner's Calling because of 'his healing' — Riven has no heal in her kit, so that line was replaced with armour priority. Chart flipped four rows in matched pairs to match the packet and the page's own whys. KIT FLAG MISFIRE: olaf.json tags Undertow with grounding, which against a three-dash champion would be the single most important fact on the page if it were true — but Riot's Undertow text is damage plus Armor and Move Speed reduction only, so nothing was written. Worth a human check: if Undertow really did ground, this matchup's advice changes materially.
